title: Regular local coordinates at a rational Tate point
statement:
For a complete field $F$ with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value and $r\geq0$, write $T_r(F)=F\langle x_1,\ldots,x_rangle$ for the ring of series $\sum_{
u\in\mathbf N^r}c_
u x^
u$ such that for every $\epsilon>0$ only finitely many $|c_
u|\geq\epsilon$, with coefficientwise addition and Cauchy multiplication. Fix $a=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\in F^r$ with $|a_i|\leq1$, and let $\operatorname{ev}_a:T_r(F)	o F$ be evaluation by convergent summation. Then $\mathfrak q=\ker(\operatorname{ev}_a)$ is the maximal ideal $(x_1-a_1,\ldots,x_r-a_r)$. Let $R=T_r(F)_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak qR$. The residue map $R	o F$ is $h/u\mapsto h(a)/u(a)$, and $R$ is a regular Noetherian local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. There is an $F$-linear isomorphism $$	heta:\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\xrightarrow{\sim}F^{\oplus r},\qquad [h/u]\longmapsto\left( rac{(\partial h/\partial x_i)(a)}{u(a)}ight)_{i=1}^r\quad(h\in\mathfrak q,\ u
otin\mathfrak q).$$ Here the partial derivatives are termwise derivatives of restricted series, and the inverse sends $(b_i)_i$ to $\sum_i b_i[x_i-a_i]$. The assertion includes $r=0$, when $R=F$ and both vector spaces are zero.

source.place: Conrad, Several approaches to non-archimedean geometry, Theorem 1.1.5(1) and Exercise 1.2.8(4), PDF pp.4 and 7 (regularity and recentering). The explicit cotangent formula is the agent-formulated first-order Taylor consequence. Read online 2026-10-24, archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $A=T_r(F)$ and introduce a second restricted-series ring $D=F\langle t_1,\ldots,t_r\rangle$. The Gauss-completion node makes both complete normed $F$-algebras. Since $\|t_i+a_i\|\le1$ and $\|x_i-a_i\|\le1$, bounded substitution gives contractive maps $\tau:A\to D$, $x_i\mapsto t_i+a_i$, and $\sigma:D\to A$, $t_i\mapsto x_i-a_i$. Their composites fix scalars and variables, so uniqueness of continuous substitution makes both composites the identity. Thus these maps are inverse isometries. Substitution in $F$ at the tuple $a$ is the given convergent evaluation, and $\operatorname{ev}_a(f)$ is the constant coefficient of $\tau(f)$: both maps are continuous algebra maps agreeing on the variables. Write $y_i=x_i-a_i$.

proof.text:
For $g=\sum c_
u t^
u\in D$ with $c_0=0$, assign each nonzero exponent $
u$ to the first $i$ with $
u_i>0$ and put its term into $t_i g_i$, where $g_i$ contains $c_
u t^{
u-e_i}$. Each $g_i$ is restricted: its coefficient family is a subfamily of that of $g$, reindexed injectively. Hence $g=\sum_i t_i g_i$. Conversely each such sum has constant coefficient zero. Applying $\sigma$ shows $\mathfrak q=(y_1,\ldots,y_r)$. Evaluation is surjective because constants map identically to $F$; its kernel is therefore maximal. In the localization $R=A_{\mathfrak q}$ the map $ho(h/u)=h(a)/u(a)$ is well-defined: the fraction relation $v(hu'-h' u)=0$, $v
otin\mathfrak q$, gives equality after evaluation and division by $v(a)u(a)u'(a)
e0$. Its kernel is precisely $\mathfrak qR$, it is onto, and the cited localization definition makes this the maximal ideal of $R$.

proof.text: Apply the affinoid-polynomial comparison node with $n=r$ and $J=0$; its Noetherian quotient is exactly $A$, so every ideal of $A$ is finitely generated. For any ideal $H\subset R$, let $I$ be its inverse image in $A$ and choose generators $f_j$ of $I$. If $h/u\in H$, then $h/1=(u/1)(h/u)\in H$, so $h\in I$ and $h/u$ is an $R$-linear combination of $f_j/1$. The reverse inclusion is immediate, proving $H=IR$ and finite generation. Thus $R$ is Noetherian. Since $\mathfrak m$ is generated by the $r$ elements $y_i/1$, the local dimension bound gives $\dim R\le r$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Conrad, Exercise 1.2.8(4) and Theorem 1.1.5(1), and the first-order Taylor consequence; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: To prove the opposite dimension bound work in $D$. For $0\le k\le r$, setting $t_1,\ldots,t_k$ to zero maps onto $F\langle t_{k+1},\ldots,t_r\rangle$ and has kernel $P_k=(t_1,\ldots,t_k)$: partition the terms containing one of the first $k$ variables as in step 2. The target is a domain. Indeed, for two nonzero series their lowest nonzero homogeneous parts multiply to a nonzero polynomial over the field, so their product has a nonzero homogeneous part. This last assertion follows from the leading-monomial multiplication of finite polynomials over a field. Thus $P_k$ is prime. Also $P_{k-1}\subsetneq P_k$, since $t_k$ survives the preceding substitution. Transport these primes by $\sigma$ to $Q_k\subseteq\mathfrak q$ in $A$. Their extensions to $R$ are prime: the quotient is a localization of the domain $A/Q_k$ at nonzero elements. Each extension contracts to $Q_k$, since $sa\in Q_k$ with $s\notin\mathfrak q$ forces $a\in Q_k$. Thus the chain remains strict, giving $\dim R\ge r$. Consequently $\dim R=r$; the $r$ generators of $\mathfrak m$ and Noetherianity prove regularity by definition.

proof.text:
For each $i$, termwise differentiation $\partial_i f=\sum_
u(
u_i+1)c_{
u+e_i}x^
u$ is restricted and is a norm-nonincreasing linear operator. Indeed $|n\cdot1|\le1$ for every natural $n$ by the nonarchimedean inequality, so the shifted differentiated coefficients still tend to zero and have norm at most $\|f\|$. Polynomial truncations converge in Gauss norm, their derivatives converge to this derivative, and evaluation and translation are contractive. The polynomial identity therefore passes to the limit: the coefficient of $t_i$ in $	au(f)$ equals $(\partial_i f)(a)$. Denote the vector of these coefficients by $L(f)$ and the constant coefficient by $c(f)=f(a)$. Finite Cauchy multiplication in degrees zero and one gives $c(fg)=c(f)c(g)$ and $L(fg)=c(f)L(g)+c(g)L(f)$. In particular $L(y_i)$ is the $i$-th standard vector.

proof.text: Use the algebra $E=F\oplus F^r$ with multiplication $(c,v)(d,w)=(cd,cw+dv)$; its second summand has square zero. The formulas in step 5 say $j(f)=(c(f),L(f))$ is an $F$-algebra map. For $u\notin\mathfrak q$, $j(u)$ has inverse $(c(u)^{-1},-c(u)^{-2}L(u))$. Thus $j_R(h/u)=j(h)j(u)^{-1}$ is a well-defined algebra map on $R$: if $v(hu'-h' u)=0$ with $v\notin\mathfrak q$, apply $j$ and cancel the three units. Its scalar component is $\rho$, so it sends $\mathfrak m$ into $0\oplus F^r$ and kills $\mathfrak m^2$. The vector component induces an $F$-linear map $\theta:\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2\to F^r$. If $h\in\mathfrak q$ its value is $L(h)/u(a)$, exactly the displayed derivative formula. This also proves independence of the chosen numerator, denominator and representative modulo $\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Agent reconstruction of Conrad, Exercise 1.2.8(4) and Theorem 1.1.5(1), and the first-order Taylor consequence; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The classes $[y_i]$ generate $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ over $F$: write $z=\sum_i r_i y_i$ using the generators of $\mathfrak m$; then $r_i-\rho(r_i)\in\mathfrak m$, so $[z]=\sum_i\rho(r_i)[y_i]$. Since $\theta([y_i])=e_i$, the map $\eta:F^r\to\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$, $(b_i)\mapsto\sum_i b_i[y_i]$, satisfies $\theta\eta=1$ and, by this spanning formula, $\eta\theta=1$. This proves the claimed isomorphism and its inverse. When $r=0$, restricted series are just $F$, evaluation is the identity, $\mathfrak q=0$, $R=F$, and $\mathfrak m=0$; the empty chain and empty sums above give dimension zero and the unique isomorphism of zero spaces.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q51-b49553324 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the new node and the report in full, and checked them against Conrad aws.pdf (fetched online and converted to text; no archive copy exists, so the report's WANTED request stands). Thm 1.1.5(1) on p.4 matches the item's regularity and dimension clause at a rational maximal ideal. Ex 1.2.8(3) on p.7 is the Banach-algebra universal property; the new node lem-per-tate-banach-substitution is its case ||b_i||<=1 with an added contractive bound. Ex 1.2.8(4) on p.7 is the recentering used in step 1. All 7 steps check out. Step 1: ||t_i+a_i||=1, and uniqueness of substitution makes tau and sigma inverse isometries with ev_a = c_0 . tau. Step 2: monomial partition gives q=(y_i), and rho is well defined. Step 3: the affinoid comparison node with J=0 gives Noetherian A, its localization is Noetherian, and dim R <= r. Step 4: the coordinate-prime chain is strict (lowest homogeneous parts give a domain) and survives localization, so dim R = r and R is regular. Step 5: |n*1|<=1 makes d_i contractive; the linear coefficient of tau(f) equals d_i f(a) by density; Leibniz holds. Step 6: inverse in the dual numbers checked; theta is F-linear and kills m^2. Step 7: spanning and both inverse identities hold, and r=0 is included. Small cases r=0, r=1, |a|=1 and char p (x^p-a^p in m^2) all behave. The new node is true, self-contained and statement-only (B1-B4 hold), and does not restate the item. I found no duplicate: lem-wf-nonarchimedean-series-substitution (one variable, values in K), lem-per-tate-maximal-residue-evaluation (residue fields only) and the trf shift calculus (formal series, char 0) say different things, and the Lean tree has no substitution declaration. None of these is a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality. I accept the two generic trf tool_uses. No changes made.
